My findings on the specific issues are as under:
10.

As the petition has been filed U/s 166 M.V Act it was incumbent upon the petitioner to prove that he sustained injuries in an accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

To determine the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle it has been held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Pushpa Rana & Another 2009 Accident Claims Journal 287 as follows:

of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of offending vehicle (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver;
(iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down.
There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on part of the driver."

It is established law that in a claim petition under Motor Vehicle Act, the standard of proof to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle is not at par with the criminal case where such rashness and negligence is required to be proved beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt.

In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act.

It was argued on behalf of the insurance company that the driver of the motorcycle and the petitioner had consumed alcohol at the time of the accident and dashed the motorcycle against the alleged offending vehicle.

A perusal of the MLC of the petitioner as well as the driver of the motorcycle Praveen Mehra shows that alcohol was present in the breath of the petitioner and of Praveen Mehra but there is nothing to show that any sample of the blood was taken to test for the quantity of alcohol in the blood of the petitioner or the driver of the motorcycle.

15. During further crossexamination PW1 had stated that at the time of the accident the driver Praveen had DL with him and in the connected case copy of DL of Praveen Mehra was placed on record.
It is pertinent that PW1 admitted that there was some construction work going on at the time of the accident.
He had volunteered that the offending vehicle was coming from the wrong side.

Though PW1 had admitted that there was some construction work going on at the time of the accident, he had stated that only the offending Suit No. D136/15 Page no. 13 of 24 Dheeraj v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors.

It is seen that the accident had taken place on the side of the petitioner as per the site plan.
It is the case of the petitioner that the offending vehicle had hit his motorcycle.

The mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle shows that the front right side rim was damaged and the tyre was torn and chimta and shocker were damaged, front right side body was damaged, front bumper and jali were damaged and the right side headlight and indicator were broken.

The mechanical inspection report of the motorcycle of the petitioner shows that right side handle and brake pedal and spot and foot rest and chassis were damaged, chain cover was damaged, back number plate was damaged as also the mudguard, seat and battery cover were broken and the right side leg guard was damaged and the front and back indicators were broken.
Thus the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident cannot be disputed.

It was stated in the FIR that the offending vehicle had come from the opposite side and hit the motorcycle of the petitioner from the side and the site plan also shows that the accident had taken place on the side of the petitioner.

The law is well settled that the compensation has to be awarded in personal injury cases under the following heads: (1) for loss of earnings during the period of treatment (2) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (3) expenses suffered by him on his treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food etc.

damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries and (2) loss of expectation of life.

sentences.text: The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and as per the same nature of injuries was opined to be simple.
The documents placed on record also do not show that the petitioner had suffered anything but simple injury though he had remained admitted in hospital.
There is also nothing to show that the petitioner had sustained any disability in the accident.
During crossexamination by the learned counsel for the insurance company PW1 stated that he remained in RML Hospital for 5 hours.
Thereafter, he was discharged from the hospital.
He admitted that he had not suffered any fracture due to the accident volunteered he had sustained injuries in his chest and internal part (5 stitches).
He admitted that he had not sustained injuries on any other part of the body except chest and internal part.
He denied the suggestion that he was discharged from RML Hospital in good condition.
He denied the suggestion that he was admitted in Behl Hospital as an afterthought to maximize the claim or that he had not required further treatment.
He denied the suggestion that he had filed false treatment record and medical bills of Behl Hospital.
He denied the suggestion that he had not spent expenses on medical bills as filed by him.
He denied the suggestion that he had suffered simple injuries.
Thus PW1 admitted that he had not suffered any fracture due to the accident and volunteered that he had sustained injuries in his chest and internal part (5 stitches).
He also admitted that he had not sustained injuries on any other part of the body except chest and internal part.
It cannot be disputed that the petitioner had sustained injuries and underwent treatment for the same.

LOSS OF INCOME 22.

It is the case of the petitioner that at the time of accident he was about 24 years old and was doing private service and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month which was handsome income to run his family but due to the accident he was on bed rest and long treatment and he lost his income and suffered from heavy loss of income as well as expenses on treatment which were continuing till date.
The petitioner in para 4 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had deposed to that effect.
He stated that after the accident his work was stopped due to long time treatment and he was suffering economic problem.
He stated that he was on bed rest for 45 months and he could not work properly, therefore, he was facing great financial losses and other irreparable losses.
However the petitioner has not placed on record any document to show what he was doing or how much amount he was earning and it was not even stated where he was doing private service.
During crossexamination by the learned counsel for the insurance company PW1 admitted that he had not filed any document to show his income and employment.
He denied the suggestion that he was not doing any job and earning Rs.15,000/ to 20,000/.
He admitted that he had not filed any medical prescription for bed rest.
He denied the suggestion that he had not suffered any financial loss due to the accident.
Thus PW1 himself stated that he had not placed on record any document to show his income and employment.

As such there is nothing to show that the petitioner was earning Rs.15,000/ to Rs.20,000/ per month at the time of the Suit No. D136/15 Page no. 20 of 24 Dheeraj v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors.

opennyai_summary.issue: Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On perusal Suit No. D136/15 Page no. 8 of 24 Dheeraj v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors.
Proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
It is established law that in a claim petition under Motor Vehicle Act, the standard of proof to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle is not at par with the criminal case where such rashness and negligence is required to be proved beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt.
Suit No. D136/15  Dheeraj v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors. 
11.
As such it cannot be said that the delay in lodging the FIR was such as would vitiate the case of the petitioner.
There is no evidence from the respondents to disprove the particulars of the accident or the involvement of vehicle No.DL8CAF3017.
In view of the testimony of PW1 and the documents on record which have remained unrebutted, the negligence of the respondent No.1 has been prima facie proved.
Thus it stands established that the petitioner had sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
Since issue No.1 has been decided in favour of the petitioner he would be entitled to compensation as per the provisions of the Act.
The law is well settled that the compensation has to be awarded in personal injury cases under the following heads: (1) for loss of earnings during the period of treatment (2) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (3) expenses suffered by him on his treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food etc.
The case of the petitioner is that due to the accident on 25.2.2015 he fell down on the road and received multiple grievous injuries.
21. Note can also be taken of the fact that on account of the accident the petitioner may not have been able to perform his day to day duties towards his family and may not have been able to enjoy the amenities of life and would have undergone pain and suffering.
No document has been placed on record regarding expenditure on conveyance, special diet or attendant charges.
Suit No. D136/15  Dheeraj v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors.
In the absence of any medical advice, note can be taken of the fact that the petitioner may not have been able to perform his avocation for some period.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs. 10,000/ consolidated on account of loss of income.
24. There is also nothing to show that the petitioner had suffered any disability on account of the injuries.
The petitioner has not proved that he acquired any disability on account of the accident or that he is likely to suffer future loss of income on account of the injuries sustained in the accident and that the injuries would reduce his efficiency to work and thereby he would Suit No. D136/15 Page no. 21 of 24 Dheeraj v Rajiv Kapoor & Ors.
suffer loss of future income.
The respondent No.1 is the driver cum owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
As such the insurance company cannot be absolved of its liability.
